performance.driver: Revenues Revenues were $3,732.4 million for the three months ended September 30, 2026, as compared with $2,967.0 million for the three months ended September 30, 2025, an increase of $765.5 million or 25.8%. The increase primarily resulted from volume growth in prescriptions dispensed within Specialty and Infusion Pharmacy partially offset by a decline in prescriptions dispensed within Home and Community Pharmacy.

Revenues Revenues were $3,732.4 million for the three months ended September 30, 2026, as compared with $2,967.0 million for the three months ended September 30, 2025, an increase of $765.5 million or 25.8%. The increase primarily resulted from volume growth in prescriptions dispensed within Specialty and Infusion Pharmacy partially offset by a decline in prescriptions dispensed within Home and Community Pharmacy.

Revenues less cost of revenues increased $4.2 million for the three months ended September 30, 2026 compared to the three months ended September 30, 2025 primarily due to an increase in net transaction and clearing fees driven by a 19% increase in Cboe Clear Europe net settlement volume.

Total revenue decreased $47 million, or 5.5%, to $809 million for the three months ended September 26, 2026, compared to $856 million for the three months ended September 27, 2025, which included net unfavorable foreign currency effects of approximately $5 million, primarily as a result of the strengthening of the United States dollar compared to the Euro.

Operating Income Operating income increased $6.2 million, or 5.6%, to $116.9 million in the three months ended September 30, 2026 compared to $110.7 million in the three months ended September 30, 2025. This increase is primarily driven by higher rental rates and average occupancy, acquisitions, and openings at Santana West, partially offset by property dispositions.

Revenues Our total revenues grew by 9.7% and 6.8%, reaching $114.3 million and $326.6 million for the three and nine months of 2026, respectively, compared to $104.2 million and $305.7 million in the prior-year periods, primarily driven by our TMT vertical.

performance.driver: Operating income (loss) Operating income for the three months ended October 3, 2026, was $187.7 million, reflecting an increase of $51.0 million, or 37.3%, compared to operating income of $136.7 million for the three months ended September 27, 2025.

Consolidated net sales for the three months ended September 30, 2026 were $507.8 million, an increase of $9.0 million, or 1.8%, compared to $498.8 million in the same period of 2025, with the majority of our net sales to customers located in the United States. The increase in Vehicle Control’s net sales was primarily driven by higher sales volume from existing customers.

Total revenues decreased by $18.5 million, or 1.6%, to $1,146.2 million for the three months ended September 30, 2026, from $1,164.7 million for the three months ended September 30, 2025. This decrease was primarily due to decreases of approximately $40.5 million and $2.1 million in the Acima and Rent-A-Center segments, respectively, partially offset by increases of approximately $21.1 million and $2.9 million in the Brigit and Mexico segments, respectively, as discussed further in the “Segment Performance” section below.

Net sales during the three months ended September 30, 2026 were approximately $2,262.5 million, or 8.6% lower than the three months ended September 30, 2025, primarily due to lower sales volumes in the Europe/Middle East and Latin America regions, most significantly in tractors, partially offset by higher sales volumes in the North America and Asia/Pacific/Africa regions, most significantly in high-horsepower tractors and hay tools.

Net revenues Net revenues for the three months ended September 30, 2026 increased $93.3 million, or 107.8%, primarily driven by negative CH-53K program adjustments of $46.0 million recorded in the prior year period compared to the reversal of $11.6 million of those adjustments in the current year period due to a contract renegotiation resulting in additional transaction price, as well as higher other program activity levels, primarily LEAP.

Operating income decreased $59.5 million and $34.2 million in the three and nine months ended September 27, 2026, respectively, from the comparable periods of 2025 primarily due to the increases in selling, general and administrative expenses; intangible asset amortization; and research and development costs, partially offset by the increase in gross profit discussed above.
Operating profit increased by $22.2 million, or 18.8%, to $140.6 million in 2026, reflecting the changes discussed above.

Income from operations for the three months ended September 30, 2026 increased by $4.4 million, or 15.6%, to $32.6 million from $28.2 million for the three months ended September 30, 2025, primarily due to higher net sales of $9.7 million, as described above, partially offset by higher SG&A expenses of $5.6 million.

Revenue per shipment increased 10% and revenue per hundredweight increased 9% in both the third quarter and in the four months ended September 30, 2026, reflecting higher fuel surcharges, favorable base yield, and increased weight per shipment.

Net Sales Net sales during the thirteen weeks ended September 24, 2026 increased $35.0 million, or 3.0%, compared to the corresponding prior year period primarily due to sales from the 20 new warehouse-format stores that we opened since September 25, 2025, partially offset by a decrease in comparable store sales of 1.4%.

Net sales decreased $363.9 million for the three months ended September 30, 2026 compared to the three months ended September 30, 2025 primarily due to a 22.0% decrease in the volume of modules sold to third parties and lower revenue associated with customer contract terminations.
Net sales for the three months ended September 30, 2026 increased by $98.3 million, or 21%, compared to the prior-year quarter, primarily due to the effects of acquisitions and pricing actions.

performance.driver: Sales and service revenues for the three months ended September 30, 2026, increased $345 million, or 11%, compared to the same period in 2025, primarily due to higher volumes at Newport News and Ingalls.

Operating Profit and Operating Profit Margin Operating profit was $817.7 million in the third quarter of 2026 compared to $434.6 million in the same period of 2025, an increase of $383.1 million, or 88.1%. The increase was primarily due to higher gross profit, as well as lower business realignment expenses, partially offset by increased SM&A expenses, as noted above.

Total revenues increased 29% in the three months ended September 30, 2026 compared to the three months ended September 30, 2025, primarily due to higher demand from leading-edge customers in memory, advanced packaging, and foundry/logic technologies, supported by continued data center investment and the adoption of AI and HPC semiconductor devices.

Net sales in the third quarter of 2026 were $544.5 million, an increase of 10% compared to $493.8 million in the third quarter of 2025. This increase was primarily driven by an increase in selling price and product mix of approximately 7% and an increase in sales volumes of approximately 3%.

Operating income increased by $47.6 million to $119.1 million for the 2026 fiscal quarter from $71.5 million for the 2025 fiscal quarter, driven by higher operating income at our Peru and Mexico segments.

Operating profit Operating profit decreased $217 million, or 9%, for the third quarter of 2026 and increased $238 million, or 3%, for the nine months ended September 30, 2026. The decrease in the third quarter was primarily driven by cost reduction program and other charges.

Operating income during the third quarter of fiscal 2026 improved by $7.6 million compared to the third quarter of fiscal 2025, primarily due to increased revenues before cost reimbursements from both our theatre division and hotels and resorts division, partially offset by an increase in corporate expenses, a $0.3 million increase in depreciation expense, and $0.2 million in impairment charges related to the planned closure of one theatre location.
Net revenues increased 2.3%, driven by by Organic Net Revenue growth of 2.1% and favorable currency-related items, partially offset by lapping prior year net revenue from a divestiture.

Sales for the nine-month period ended September 30, 2026 were favorably affected by increased sales within the following platforms: (a) Access, which increased by $32.8 million, or 7.5%, from the corresponding period of 2025. This increase was driven primarily by hemostasis products acquired in the Biolife Merger, as well as increased sales of our angiography and access products, partially offset by decreased sales in our drainage products.
Operating income increased $83 million (2.6%), due primarily to higher OCI.

performance.driver: Total revenues increased 7% to $276.5 million compared to $258.5 million in the third quarter of 2025, driven by a 3.3% increase in average guest spend, fleet expansion due to 2026 vessel newbuilds, and higher volumes, primarily reflecting a 1.8% increase in revenue days net of 2026 fleet expansion and an increase in guest count, contributing $8.2 million, $7.0 million and $4.3 million, respectively, to the increase in total revenues for the period.

Revenues Used vehicle retail sales revenue increased from 2025 to 2026 due to a $106.8 million, or 4.8%, increase in same-store revenues, partially offset by a $22.1 million decrease from net dealership acquisitions/dispositions.

Net sales of $209.5 million increased $31.4 million for the three months ended September 30, 2026 year-over-year and net sales of $598.5 million increased $102.2 million for the nine months ended September 30, 2026 year-over-year, mainly due to an increase in energy and, to a lesser extent, communications sales, led by PLP-USA.

Net Sales Product sales decreased $4.0 million, or 0.9%, for the three months ended September 30, 2026, compared to the three months ended September 30, 2025, primarily due to a $6.2 million decrease in paper sales, partially offset by $2.0 million in favorable foreign exchange impacts and a $0.2 million increase in net sales.

Revenue grew from $103.4 million for the three months ended September 30, 2025 to $112.1 million for the three months ended September 30, 2026, an increase of $8.6 million or 8%. The increase in revenue was driven primarily by growth in our subscription revenue of $7.5 million for the three months ended September 30, 2026 compared to the three months ended September 30, 2025.

Revenue increased by $107.9 million, or 39%, to $385.8 million for the three months ended September 30, 2026 as compared to $277.9 million for the same period in 2025. The increase was mainly due to and directly correlated with our continued growth across existing markets.

Revenue Revenue for the three months ended September 30, 2026 was $816.0 million, compared to $743.0 million for the three months ended September 30, 2025, an increase of $73.0 million. The increase was driven principally by organic growth of $45.7 million, or 7.4%, and $4.3 million from acquisitions, net of dispositions, partially offset by a $0.5 million unfavorable impact from foreign currency.

Consolidated revenue increased $1.5 million for the three months ended September 30, 2026 compared to the three months ended September 30, 2025. The increase was primarily driven by higher OTT revenue resulting from subscription price increases and higher distribution and other revenue related to international ancillary market sales of Fightland Season 1 and the transition of our Canadian operations to a content licensing relationship.

Total revenue was $605.1 million for the three months ended September 30, 2026, compared to $626.4 million for the three months ended September 30, 2025, a decrease of $21.3 million, or 3%. This decrease in revenue was driven by lower revenue in our BetterHelp segment, reflecting continued actions to prioritize Insurance Covered Services and the continuing decline in users paying directly out of pocket, partially offset by higher revenue in our Integrated Care segment.

Revenues Same‑hospital net operating revenues increased by $247 million, or 6.2%, and by $496 million, or 4.1%, during the three and nine months ended September 30, 2026, respectively, driven by higher patient volumes as well as continued pricing strength, partially offset by a less favorable payer mix.

Net sales were $7.2 billion for the third quarter of 2026 compared to $6.2 billion for the third quarter of 2025, an increase of 16.6%. This growth reflects an approximate 14% increase in volume driven by all three segments (CSS, EES and UBS), and an approximate 3% benefit from price.

Consolidated net sales increased by $69.9 million, or 8.7%, for the three months ended September 30, 2026, as compared to the same period in 2025, including an unfavorable foreign currency translation impact of $4.0 million and a reduction in SmartDose® 3.5mL product revenue of $18.0 million due to our sale of the product line to AbbVie on July 1, 2026.

Revenue Total revenue increased $104 million, or 3%, in the third quarter of 2026, compared to the prior-year period. The increase reflects 6% organic revenue growth, driven by net new business and ongoing strong retention, partially offset by a 3% unfavorable impact primarily from divestitures largely due to the sales of the NFP Wealth business and Stroz Friedberg.

Revenue increased by $2 million, or 200%, to $3 million in the three months ended September 30, 2026 from $1 million in the three months ended September 30, 2025, primarily due to increased utilization, geographical expansion, and higher fuel surcharges.
